text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The opposition Fatherland Union submitted a draft law calling for an increase of income tax exemptions for families with children.
- Swedish and Estonian foreign ministers to sign a preliminary agreement on visa-free travel in Stockholm.
- The interior ministry is preparing an information booklet for travellers to the countries which do not require visas.
- The daily described the preparations for the concert of the pop star Michael Jackson and his requirements to the organisers. Jackson will perform in Tallinn on August 22.
- U.S. officials promised to an Estonian delegation that the U.S. will never agree to Estonia becoming part of a Russian sphere of influence.
- Estonian TV was fined for failure to provide Estonian titles to Russian-language news broadcast.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann said that the appointment of another minister to the cabinet will be decided next week. The minister's sphere of responsibility is not yet clear.
- Russia is ready to return the Estonian president's badge of office, which has been kept in a Kremlin museum since 1940, Russian Culture Minister Yevgeni Sidorov said.

- Research firm Saar Poll studies Estonian entrepreneurs and found that the managers of large Tallinn-based firms with foreign participation are the most active supporters of liberal market economy. Managers of rural or smaller enterprises prefer a social market economy.
